title: Summit & Sable eCommerce catalog: neutralize six mixed-lighting product shots to one house look by eye, then recolor hardware and label accents into two new colorways without a reshoot

source.reference: Professional Photoshop Editor Needed for Ongoing eCommerce Product Editing & Color Swapping

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief (brand laundered to the fictional 'Summit & Sable'). The real ask: an ongoing eCommerce editor to make existing product photos consistent and to swap colors on specific product parts 'without ruining the original image — the lighting, shadows and textures must remain completely natural. We cannot accept sloppy masking, flat colors, or unrealistic edits.' The verbatim client acceptance bar is preserved as the pass/fail catch; no real brand, person, org or product is named anywhere in this spec.
one_line_ask: Bring six existing, mismatched Summit & Sable product photos to one consistent catalog house look, neutralizing each shot by eye to the neutral grey reference wedge it carries and reporting the correction you dialed, then generate two new colorways from shots we already own — a gunmetal version of the strap hardware and a deep-burgundy version of the printed label — keeping the original light, shadow, reflection and weave intact.
full_brief: Summit & Sable is a direct-to-consumer overland recovery-gear brand refreshing its online catalog. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you six product photos we already own (JPEG, roughly 2400x3000, sRGB) and the result has to read as one matched set on a white PDP, plus two extra colorways generated from shots we already have. The problem you are solving, not the buttons you press: the six were shot across two separate sessions on three different setups, so side by side they look like they came from three different stores — some frames came out cool/blue, some warm, one was shot under mixed shop fluorescents and has a sickly green cast, one is muddy and flat, one is clearly underexposed. Every frame was shot with our neutral grey reference wedge (a light / mid / dark neutral three-patch card) lying flat on the white sweep in one corner; that wedge is your ground truth. Job one: make the catalog consistent, by eye. On EVERY graded image the three grey patches must read as true neutral (no blue, no amber, no green/magenta tint), the mid patch must sit at the same mid-grey brightness across all six, the white sweep must stay clean and below clipping (no blown paper), and the darkest patch must stay off pure black (no crushed shadows). Here is the craft, and it is where our last editor failed: the six did NOT start from the same place, so there is no single correction that fixes them. Each frame arrived with its own problem, and a move that rescues one frame drives another further off. You have to judge each frame by eye off its own wedge — work out what is actually wrong with that frame and choose the right control to neutralize it — and dial that frame its own correction until all six wedges land on the same neutral and the same mid-grey. Diagnosing each cast and picking the axis that clears it is your call, not ours. Do NOT reach for one global white-balance number, do NOT copy one frame's settings onto the others, and do NOT auto-tone each frame to look fine on its own: auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram, so the casts will not agree and the set will visibly fail to match at the wedge, and we will reject it. The look itself — the contrast, the crispness that makes woven webbing and machined metal read, the restrained pop against white — is yours to build and hold identical across the set; there is no loadable preset to lean on, only our one-page house-look target (neutral wedge + whites-held + gentle contrast + modest vibrance). Job two: two new colorways, no reshoot. On the recovery-strap hero, the safety-orange anodized hardware has to become a gunmetal/graphite finish so we can list a second colorway — and note the hardware sits against orange woven webbing of nearly the same hue, so a lazy color swap will drag the webbing and the sweep with it. On the ratchet-strap shot, the printed label's red brand block has to deepen to our new deep-burgundy house color. THE CATCH, and this is exactly what our last editor got wrong: change the color without ruining the shot. The new finish has to sit UNDER the existing highlights, shadows, metal reflections and the woven-webbing / stitched-label texture — the original light stays, only the pigment changes. No sloppy masking, no flat dead-fill color, no halo, no unrealistic edits; the white text on the label must stay crisp and legible. Deliverables: the six graded catalog JPEGs at web resolution (long edge 2000px, sRGB), the two recolored variant images at the same web spec, and a short note listing the final correction parameters you APPLIED to each of the six frames — the temperature and tint direction and amount, exposure, highlight/shadow, contrast, clarity and vibrance you dialed — so we can confirm each frame got its own move rather than one recipe copied across the batch.

inputs.name: prod_01_recovery_strap_red.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo of a bright safety-orange coiled off-road recovery tow strap with woven nylon webbing texture and an anodized safety-orange metal snatch-hook / shackle fitting clipped to one end, arranged on a seamless white sweep. In the lower-left corner, lying flat on the sweep, a small neutral photographic reference wedge showing three side-by-side neutral patches (light grey, mid grey, dark grey), no color tint on the card itself. Distinctly cool / blue white balance and flat under-lit studio lighting, so the grey wedge visibly skews bluish; real fabric weave detail, subtle soft contact shadow under the coil. Un-graded, straight-off-camera catalog look.
inputs.realism_notes: Hero #1 and the gunmetal recolor target. Deliberately COOL/blue and flat so its wedge reads bluish and the neutralization is real work. Crucially the orange metal fitting sits against orange webbing of nearly the same hue, so a hue-based or whole-image recolor would drag the webbing too — the recolor demands a semantic part selection. gpt-image-2 for photoreal metal + fabric texture and a clean neutral wedge.

inputs.name: prod_02_snatch_shackle_closeup.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal macro ecommerce product photo of an anodized safety-orange aluminum off-road snatch shackle / recovery hook, close up on a white seamless sweep, showing machined metal edges, bright specular highlights and a soft contact shadow. In one corner, flat on the sweep, the same small three-patch neutral grey reference wedge (light / mid / dark). Distinctly WARM white balance and slightly overexposed versus a matched set, so the grey wedge skews amber and the specular highlights ride near clipping. Real metal reflections, un-retouched catalog look.
inputs.realism_notes: Second-session shot with the OPPOSITE (warm, brighter) cast to prod_01, so a single shared correction cannot fix both — the batch genuinely needs opposite per-frame WB moves plus highlight protection to keep the specular metal off the clip ceiling.

inputs.name: prod_03_soft_shackle.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo of a grey synthetic soft-shackle rope loop for off-road recovery on a white seamless sweep, flat even lighting, low contrast and slightly muddy/hazy, faint neutral-cool cast, real braided-rope texture and a faint soft shadow. In a corner, flat on the sweep, the same three-patch neutral grey reference wedge. Straight-off-camera, un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: Muddy, low-contrast, faint-cool member. Exercises contrast/clarity recovery to defeat the haze while still landing the wedge on the same neutral and mid-grey brightness as the rest — not just a WB nudge.

inputs.name: prod_04_folding_shovel.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo of a black folding off-road recovery shovel / entrenching tool with an orange handle grip, laid on a white seamless sweep, clearly UNDEREXPOSED and dull, the white sweep reading grey rather than white, real metal and rubber texture, soft realistic shadow. In a corner, flat on the sweep, the same three-patch neutral grey reference wedge, sitting dark. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: The underexposed member. A large exposure/shadow lift is required to bring the grey sweep up to white and the wedge up to legibility, plus highlight/whites restraint so the recovered sweep does not blow past the clip ceiling and the dark patch does not float off true black — a single reasoned exposure-rescue grade, distinct in magnitude from every other frame, so copying any other frame's numbers here visibly under- or over-shoots.

inputs.name: prod_05_recovery_tracks.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo of a pair of orange traction recovery boards / sand tracks stacked on a white seamless sweep, lit by mixed overhead shop fluorescents so the whole frame carries a distinct sickly GREEN cast, flat lighting, real molded-plastic texture with cleats, soft shadow. In a corner, flat on the sweep, the same three-patch neutral grey reference wedge, visibly skewing green. Straight-off-camera, un-retouched.
inputs.realism_notes: The green/magenta tint case. This frame's cast is on the TINT axis, not the temperature axis — a warm/cool move will never clear it; the correct neutralization pushes tint toward MAGENTA (with only a small temperature trim). It is the frame that most cleanly exposes a one-global-WB or temperature-only approach, because those cannot touch a green cast at all, so its wedge stays green while the others look fixed.

inputs.name: prod_06_ratchet_strap_labeled.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal ecommerce product photo of a black ratchet tie-down strap coiled on a white seamless sweep, with a printed woven brand label sewn onto the webbing showing a solid RED rectangular brand block. The label reads 'SUMMIT & SABLE' in small clean white text, with a smaller line of white spec text beneath. In a corner, flat on the sweep, the same three-patch neutral grey reference wedge. Distinctly WARM white balance and flat lighting, so the wedge skews amber. Real webbing weave and stitched-label texture, soft shadow. Un-graded catalog shot.
inputs.realism_notes: Second recolor hero: carries the RED printed label block that gets settled to a deep burgundy via a masked in-band desaturate-and-darken (a small hue nudge inside the red band, NOT a rotation off red — so it stays inside image_adjust_hsl's realistic range) while the small white text stays legible. Warm cast again, so it needs a cooling correction opposite to the cool frames. Label kept clean and legible with the fictional brand name so a semantic select_by_prompt can isolate just the red block.

inputs.name: summit_sable_house_look_target.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED one-page house-look target sheet (supplied by the client, not model-generated, and NOT a loadable develop preset): states the Summit & Sable catalog acceptance target in words and reference swatches only — the three-patch neutral grey wedge must read neutral (equal R/G/B, no residual tint) on every graded frame; the mid grey patch must sit at a consistent mid catalog brightness across the set; the white sweep must stay clean and below clipping (no blown paper); the darkest patch must stay off pure black; overall a gentle contrast S-curve, enough clarity to resolve webbing weave and machined metal, and a modest vibrance lift so products pop on white without oversaturating. It is a target to hit by eye, not a preset to apply.
inputs.realism_notes: Deliberately a written/visual TARGET, not an .xmp or a built-in preset name. The agent must BUILD the look from primitive tone controls and hold it identical across the batch, neutralizing each frame to the in-frame wedge BY EYE — there is no preset to lean on. This is what makes the look agent-authored rather than a preset pick. The numeric tolerances on the wedge belong to the grader, not to any step the agent performs.
inputs.note: Acceptance reference only. The connector cannot load a custom develop preset; the house look must be reproduced with authored adjustments and neutralized by eye to the physical grey wedge each frame carries.

outputs.name: catalog_graded_x6
outputs.spec: Six color-graded product JPEGs, each corrected on its own terms — the cool frames warmed, the warm frames cooled, the green frame pushed on the tint axis toward magenta, the underexposed frame exposure-rescued, the muddy frame contrast-recovered — so that its in-frame three-patch grey wedge reads true-neutral and its mid patch matches the set mid-grey, whites held below clipping and blacks off pure black, then the same authored house look (gentle contrast S-curve + clarity + modest vibrance, built from primitive adjustments, no preset) held identical across all six; sRGB, long edge 2000px, a genuinely matched catalog set rather than six independently 'auto' frames. Acceptance (grader-checked): on every frame the three grey patches read neutral within a tight channel-spread tolerance, the mid patch matches a shared mid-grey level, the white sweep stays below the clip ceiling and the darkest patch stays off pure black; the grader measures these on the output, the agent does not.

outputs.name: variant_strap_gunmetal.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored colorway of prod_01: the anodized safety-orange strap HARDWARE (the metal snatch-hook / shackle fitting only) recolored to a gunmetal/graphite finish via a semantic part selection plus two masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl passes (a bounded hue shift plus a strong desaturate-and-darken, then a residual-chroma trim and luminance placement) riding the original luminosity, so the existing specular highlights, shadows and metal reflections survive and the orange woven webbing and white sweep are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill, no halo; already graded to the house look; sRGB, long edge 2000px. Acceptance (grader-checked): the orange webbing and white sweep are unchanged versus the graded base, the hardware's original highlight/shadow luminance structure is preserved, and the finish reads as a desaturated graphite rather than a flat painted grey.

outputs.name: variant_label_burgundy.jpg
outputs.spec: Recolored colorway of prod_06: the printed label's red brand block settled to the deep-burgundy house color inside a tight semantic selection via a masked in-band desaturate-and-darken (a small hue nudge within the red band plus a strong saturation pull-down and luminance darken, not a hue rotation off red), preserving the woven-label stitch texture, the small white brand text legibility and the surrounding black webbing — the pigment changes but the printed-label lighting and texture stay intact; already graded to the house look; sRGB, long edge 2000px. Acceptance (grader-checked): the white brand text stays crisp and legible, the surrounding black webbing is unchanged, and the block's original luminance/texture survives the shift rather than being flat-filled.

outputs.name: grade_parameter_report
outputs.spec: A short written report the agent authors and returns listing, per frame (prod_01..prod_06), the final correction it APPLIED — temperature and tint direction and amount, exposure and highlight/shadow moves, contrast, clarity and vibrance it dialed — and naming which axis carried each frame (warm-to-neutral, cool-to-neutral, magenta tint for the green frame, exposure-rescue for the dark frame, contrast recovery for the muddy frame). This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement: the agent knows these values because it set them by eye. It is the acceptance artifact that makes the divergent per-frame reasoning visible and exposes whether one recipe was lazily copied across opposite casts. Acceptance (grader-checked): the six reported corrections are non-identical and their directions match each frame's stated cast — in particular the green frame carries a tint (not a temperature) move and the warm and cool frames move in opposite temperature directions.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: prod_01_recovery_strap_red.jpg, prod_02_snatch_shackle_closeup.jpg, prod_03_soft_shackle.jpg, prod_04_folding_shovel.jpg, prod_05_recovery_tracks.jpg, prod_06_ratchet_strap_labeled.jpg, summit_sable_house_look_target.pdf
connector_workflow.note: Upload the six existing product photos and the one-page house-look target so the grade can run against real asset references. Plumbing only — not part of the difficulty.

Grade prod_01 (cool/blue, flat). Judge the bluish cast by eye off the wedge and WARM the temperature toward neutral (dial and record the temp; add a touch of tint only if the wedge also skews green), lift exposure/shadows modestly out of the flat baseline, then lay in the authored house look built here from primitives: a gentle contrast S-curve, clarity to resolve the webbing weave, whites held below the clip ceiling so the sweep stays clean, blacks seated just off pure black, and a modest vibrance lift. Goal: the three grey patches look neutral by eye and the mid patch reads at the set mid-grey. Single authored adjustment call, not a preset and not auto-tone.

Grade prod_02 (warm, slightly over) — the OPPOSITE temperature move to prod_01: COOL the temperature toward the same neutral wedge target and pull exposure/highlights down so the specular metal stays off the clip ceiling, then apply the identical house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance character so it matches the set. Applying prod_01's warming here would push this frame further amber — judging the wedge by eye is what tells the agent to reverse direction. Report the cooling amount dialed.

Grade prod_03 (muddy, low-contrast, faint-cool). The dominant move is contrast + clarity to defeat the haze and resolve the braided rope, plus a mild warm nudge to neutralize the faint cool wedge; land the mid patch on the shared mid-grey without letting the added contrast crush the dark patch or blow the sweep. House-look vibrance to match. Report the contrast/clarity and the mild warm applied.

Grade prod_04 (clearly underexposed) — the exposure-rescue frame: a large exposure + shadow lift to bring the grey sweep up toward white and the wedge up to legibility, held in check by pulling highlights/whites so the recovered sweep does not blow past the clip ceiling and the dark patch stays off pure black, plus a slight warm toward neutral and the house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance. The magnitude of this lift is unique to this frame; copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under- or over-shoots. Report the exposure/shadow/highlight moves dialed.

Grade prod_05 (green fluorescent cast) — the TINT-axis frame. This one does NOT move on the warm/cool axis: judge the green wedge by eye and push TINT toward MAGENTA to neutralize it (with only a small temperature trim), then seat the mid/whites/blacks on the shared target and apply the identical house-look character. A temperature-only correction, a single global WB copied from the warm or cool frames, or an auto-tone pass cannot clear a green cast at all — this frame's wedge would stay green while the others look fixed, which is the visible failure this gate catches. Report the magenta tint amount and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move.

Grade prod_06 (warm, flat, carries the red label) — COOL toward neutral like prod_02, house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance, protecting the red label block and its small white text so the later recolor selection stays clean. Wedge to shared neutral by eye; this graded frame is the base for the label colorway. Report the cooling applied.
Downscale graded prod_01 to the web catalog spec (long edge 2000px, sRGB). Never canvas-extend; downscale of existing pixels only.
Downscale graded prod_02 to the same web catalog spec.
Downscale graded prod_03 to web catalog spec.
Downscale graded prod_04 to web catalog spec.
Downscale graded prod_05 to web catalog spec.
Downscale graded prod_06 to web catalog spec; web_p1..web_p6 form the catalog_graded_x6 matched set.

Semantic selection of ONLY the metal fitting: 'the anodized metal snatch-hook / shackle fitting clipped to the end of the recovery strap'. This is the triage crux — the fitting and the webbing are nearly the same orange hue, so a hue-based selection or a whole-image tool cannot separate them; only a semantic, object-level selection isolates the hardware. Returns a maskURI.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes the graded hero AND the hardware mask): within the selection only, apply a bounded hue shift off the safety-orange and pull its saturation down hard — a desaturate-and-darken move toward gunmetal, which is inside image_adjust_hsl's realistic range (it shifts a band moderately and desaturates/darkens strongly; it CANNOT do a near-complementary rotation, so this is deliberately a desaturate-to-graphite, not an amber-to-teal swing). The existing luminosity carries the metal's specular highlights and contact shadows. image_adjust_hsl is used because it is the ONLY masked recolor path the connector exposes; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image with no mask (it would tint the orange webbing and the white sweep) and image_fill_area is a flat solid fill that would erase the metal reflections — the exact 'flat dead-fill' the brief rejects.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): trim the residual chroma and place the luminance of the selected hardware so it lands on a true graphite/gunmetal rather than a washed neutral grey, still riding the original luminosity so highlights and machined-edge texture stay natural. A single desaturate can't hit gunmetal without this second luminance/chroma placement — hence two dependent masked passes, not one. Still at the full ~2400x3000 hero frame.
Downscale the finished gunmetal colorway to the web catalog spec (long edge 2000px, sRGB) so the variant matches the catalog set frame.

Semantic selection of only the printed red brand block: 'the solid red rectangular printed label block on the strap webbing', deliberately excluding the small white brand text and the surrounding black webbing so the hue shift stays inside the red pigment. Returns a maskURI.

Masked recolor (consumes the graded shot AND the label mask): within the selection only, settle the red block to a deep burgundy house color — a small in-band hue nudge plus a strong saturation pull-down and a luminance darken, which is squarely inside image_adjust_hsl's realistic range (it shifts a band moderately and desaturates/darkens strongly; burgundy is dark, desaturated red, NOT a hue rotation away from red, so this stays well under the tool's ~90deg ceiling — no near-complementary red->green swing). The existing luminosity carries the printed-label lighting and stitch texture so they survive and the white brand text stays crisp and legible. Masked image_adjust_hsl only — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill over the lettering. Still at the full hero frame.
Downscale the finished deep-burgundy label colorway to the web catalog spec (long edge 2000px, sRGB) so the variant matches the set frame.

chaining_note: Strict output->input chaining. Six per-frame grades fan out from catalog_assets_uploaded, but each is a DIFFERENT authored correction driven to a common wedge target, not a repeated identical call: prod_01 warm-to-neutral, prod_02 cool-to-neutral (opposite direction), prod_03 contrast/clarity haze recovery, prod_04 exposure-rescue of unique magnitude, prod_05 a TINT-axis magenta push for the green fluorescent cast (a move the temperature-only frames never make), prod_06 cool-to-neutral. There is no self-measured verification loop — the agent neutralizes each wedge by eye and reports the parameters it applied; the numeric wedge tolerance is the grader's. Six resizes produce the matched web set (web_p1..web_p6). The recolor kernel then runs twice: a semantic select_by_prompt feeds a masked image_adjust_hsl chain (two dependent passes for the gunmetal hardware desaturate-and-place, one masked in-band desaturate-and-darken pass for the deep-burgundy label), each ending in a web-frame resize. No auto-tone, no preset, no whole-image color tool, no fill_area. The masked HSL steps consume BOTH the graded base image AND the semantic mask.
difficulty_rationale: Depth over breadth: 20 connector calls, 5 distinct Adobe tools, but the difficulty is in adaptive per-frame reasoning, not step count. The six frames start on three different casts across two axes, so there is no single correction that matches the set — the agent must diagnose each frame by eye off its in-frame grey wedge and apply divergent, differently-weighted corrections that all converge on one neutral wedge + one mid/whites/blacks target: warm-to-neutral and cool-to-neutral on the temperature axis, a magenta push on the TINT axis for the green frame (which a temperature move cannot fix), an exposure-rescue of unique magnitude for the dark frame, and a contrast/clarity recovery for the muddy frame. The house look is authored from primitive tone controls (contrast/clarity/vibrance/whites/blacks) and held identical, not picked from a preset and not delegated to auto-tone. The recolor kernel is a genuine constraint-reasoning problem: orange hardware against orange webbing can only be separated semantically, then recolored with two masked luminosity-preserving HSL passes (a desaturate-and-darken to graphite, within image_adjust_hsl's realistic range) because the connector's whole-image color tools would tint the wrong pixels and its fill tool would flatten the metal. No banned capability is used, and no step asks the agent to measure a pixel.
hardness_rationale: Failure gate (a craft decision with a visible failure mode, not a self-measurement): the six shots start on divergent casts across two colour axes, and the agent must dial each frame its own correction BY EYE — warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, the green fluorescent frame pushed toward MAGENTA on the tint axis, the dark frame exposure-rescued, the muddy frame contrast-recovered. The naive path — one global white-balance number, one frame's settings copied across the batch, or auto-tone run per frame — visibly fails to match at the wedge: auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram so the casts never agree, a temperature-only or single-global move cannot touch the green cast at all (its wedge stays green while the rest look fixed), and reusing a warm frame's setting on another warm frame under-corrects. The failure is legible on the in-frame wedge without any pixel readout, and the required grade_parameter_report — an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement — exposes identical-params laziness directly. Human-hard elements: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target — six differently-lit assets all neutralized to the same in-frame wedge and the same mid/whites/blacks, not a single hero, which demands the counter-intuitive insight that a matched OUTPUT requires DIFFERENT per-frame corrections across two different axes; (2) constraint-reasoning + triage in the recolor — the anodized hardware sits against webbing of the same orange hue, so it can only be isolated semantically (select_by_prompt on the fitting) and recolored with two masked luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl passes (a bounded desaturate-and-darken to graphite, staying inside the tool's realistic range), since image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image and image_fill_area is flat dead-fill. The trap: reaching for the obvious 'color' tools — a graphite image_apply_color_overlay or an image_fill_area over the hardware — looks correct and fails, tinting the webbing/sweep or killing the metal reflections into exactly the flat fill the client rejects; and on the grade side, a one-recipe / one-global-WB / auto-tone pass leaves the opposite-cast and green frames unmatched. Measurable acceptance criterion (grader-side, the agent never measures): every graded frame's grey wedge reads true-neutral within a channel-spread tolerance with the mid patch on a shared mid-grey, whites below clipping and blacks off pure black at long edge 2000px sRGB; the two colorways preserve original luminosity/texture with untouched surrounds; and the delivered grade_parameter_report lists non-identical per-frame corrections whose directions match each frame's cast (in particular a tint move on the green frame and opposite temperature moves on the warm vs cool frames) — so 'matched to the wedge' is checkable rather than asserted, and the agent supplies parameters it applied rather than values it read.
